rows.title: Check the brain’s own representations for disagreement
rows.conclusion: Micah's July 2022 Git-recorded discussion proposes checking internal representations by sampling and cross-referencing them to notice inconsistency. MCH's reviewed version likewise makes conflicts between partial models a focus of conscious attention; the common subchain is comparison and discrepancy detection, not an equation of rarity with contradiction.

SAN.date_type: Locally verified Git author and committer timestamps of byte-matching blob; not independently timestamped first-public availability
SAN.quote: Is there a way for a natural brain to check its own results, to check for pattern representation accuracy. one way to do that would be to sort of do to take multiple samples like sort of like with with and cross reference them, it's like, okay well I'm gonna attack multiple times and if something is true then it's gonna be true.
SAN.summary: SAN proposes taking and cross-checking samples of the brain’s own representations. Disagreement can then be noticed instead of simply passed along.
SAN.source_context: The rare-pattern statement explicitly invokes information theory. The later same-file checking discussion supplies the consistency operation; the review does not silently equate rarity with model contradiction or treat Shannon's general principle as a SAN invention.

rows.title: Build an internal world, then register it again
rows.conclusion: Micah's September 2022 Git-recorded account builds experienced self and world from contrasts in a continuing field and makes rendered patterns available to the brain again. MCH's reviewed Genesis passage also builds represented space, objects and self through differences, alongside reflexive perception. This supports a shared construction narrative, not the same neural mechanism.

SAN.date_type: Locally verified Git author and committer timestamps of byte-matching blob; not independently timestamped first-public availability
SAN.quote: The brain is effectively doing computational rendering & then reading it’s own output pattern, from neuronal outputs, as that pattern is looped or played back to the neural network of the brain which detects it, with neuronal inputs, and re-renders (outputs it again) with new sensor input data.
SAN.summary: SAN proposes that differences in ongoing activity form a represented self and world. The brain receives its own rendered patterns again and updates them with new input.
SAN.source_context: The September text explicitly includes bursts, inhibition and slow-wave departures, not excitation alone. The review isolates the proposed functional chain without treating every anatomical or frequency claim as experimentally established.

CIMC's reviewed whitepaper asks whether developmental trajectories show predicted transitions alongside new internal organization. This is a shared developmental test direction, not an equation of synaptic phase with developmental phase transitions.

SAN.date_type: Locally verified Git author and committer timestamps of byte-matching blob; not independently timestamped first-public availability
SAN.quote: Imagine that Synaptic Connections via Growth LTP & Decay LTD, over a long term, results in eventual threshold changes that we can identify as Stages, or major changes in live perspective that only happen after a very long time, or only happen after a very big life event.
SAN.summary: SAN distinguishes short-lived experiences from slower changes in neural organization. It applies that distinction to the development of artificial minds.
SAN.source_context: The source explicitly attributes the general states/stages concept to AQAL or Spiral Dynamics. Its SAN proposal connects that distinction to synaptic phase, growth/decay and artificial realization. The exact mature wording is November 2022, not a June heading.

target.title: Consciousness Is Model Coherence
target.date_type: Selected document-version date, not proof this wording appeared in the initial publication
target.summary: The later whitepaper asks whether a developing system shows transitions alongside new internal organization. SAN’s earlier threshold-stage proposal supports this particular comparison.

rows.shared_subchain: Observe an artificial system's developmental trajectory for changes in internal organization, including threshold-like transitions associated with new capacities.

L1.reasoning: Supported partial transition/assessment mapping: November9 explicitly proposes threshold changes in stages from accumulated growth/decay; CIMC18 asks whether developmental trajectories show predicted phase transitions and links marked cross-modal improvement to emergent internal structures.
L1.formal_ceiling: No proved mathematical isomorphism, bisimulation, functor or implementation equivalence; theoretical correspondence is not experimental validation.

L2.reasoning: November ongoing experience and slow connection change -> qualitative stage -> mature artificial mind corresponds to CIMC self-organization/developmental pressure -> emergent organization and improved integration -> evidence to evaluate. Different causes remain visible.

L3.reasoning: Reverse from a newly organized artificial cognitive capacity: developmental evidence and qualitative changes matter. November supplies a threshold-stage antecedent; frequency phase and dynamical developmental phase transition are not interchangeable.

Earlier source and target routes remain open; no unique derivation, independent first-publication proof, whole-program firstness or influence follows.

rows.residual: CIMC's phase transitions are not specified as synaptic phase shifts or LTP/LTD, and November does not establish the target's coherence-plus-metarepresentation transition. General states/stages is acknowledged background from AQAL/Spiral Dynamics.

rows.title: Perception can include the act of perceiving
rows.conclusion: Micah's July 2022 Git-recorded discussion explicitly locates perceiving perception in neural operations, alongside internally rendered patterns received again. MCH's reviewed version also characterizes consciousness through perception that perception occurs. The partial reflexive correspondence does not establish identical timing or representational structure.

SAN.quote: the one process in the machine is always seeking to know, it's always seeking to know is perceiving perception.
SAN.summary: SAN explicitly discusses perceiving perception as a neural process. Its account includes internally rendered patterns being received again.
SAN.source_context: The source's explicit phrase is embedded in an account of multimodal coincidence, representation checking and neural-array rendering. A following receiver by itself does not prove same-level metarepresentation; this is tested as a partial reflexive-perception proposal.

target.title: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis
target.date_type: Selected document-version date, not proof this wording appeared in the initial publication
target.summary: The later paper also describes perception that perception is occurring. The shared reflexive function does not establish identical timing or structure.

rows.shared_subchain: A neural/computational process registers its own perceptual activity, with internal representations available to further perception rather than an unexplained outside viewer.

L1.reasoning: July195 explicitly characterizes a neural mechanism as perceiving perception;31 supplies neural-array output received by another array and159 checking one's own results. MCH15 explicitly perceives that perception is occurring. This supports a partial reflexive function beyond a generic feed-forward receiver.
L1.formal_ceiling: No proved mathematical isomorphism, bisimulation, functor or implementation equivalence; theoretical correspondence is not experimental validation.

L2.reasoning: July rendered multimodal pattern -> subsequent reception/checking -> acknowledgment/perceiving perception aligns with MCH structured percept -> contemporaneous registration of observing. The source's ordered next-array story is not proof of subjective simultaneity.

L3.reasoning: Reverse from awareness of perceiving: the system must make its own perceptual activity available to a perceptual process. July supplies that stated objective and candidate operation, not the complete sufficient conditions for second-order phenomenology.
L3.chronological_constraint: Only this exact 2022-07-06T20:15:38-07:00 Git-record-dated formulation is compared against the selected 2026-01-15 target version. Earlier source and target routes remain open; no unique derivation, independent first-publication proof, whole-program firstness or influence follows.

rows.residual: A following receiver alone could process content without representing that perception occurs. July does not establish MCH's immediate non-inferential synchronous form, and its self-as-direction (187) is not MCH's full observing-self model.

rows.title: Choose the detail a simulation needs to preserve
rows.conclusion: Micah's November 2022 Git-recorded implementation proposal models individual dendrites, synapses and their changing dynamics. MCH's reviewed version likewise raises the possibility that simulating consciousness needs more cellular detail than simplified neuron-to-neuron messages. Neither establishes the required resolution experimentally.

SAN.date_type: Locally verified Git author and committer timestamps of byte-matching blob; not independently timestamped first-public availability
SAN.quote: The essential physics process could be simulated in just matrix calculations on a TPU, with each dendrite, each neuron, each synapse, and each cortical column being unique or random in it's original configuration
SAN.summary: SAN proposes modeling dendrites, synapses, neurons and larger assemblies with changing spatial and temporal responses.
SAN.source_context: The source compares FPGA/GPU/TPU and neuromorphic options as speculative implementation routes. It names dendrites and synapses explicitly but does not require simulation of every biochemical process.

target.title: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis
target.date_type: Selected document-version date, not proof this wording appeared in the initial publication
target.summary: The later paper raises the possibility that simplified messages between neurons may omit important cellular machinery. Both question what detail a simulation needs.

rows.shared_subchain: A simulation meant to realize consciousness may need to retain computational detail below a simplified whole-neuron unit; preserve relevant component organization rather than assume a coarse network is sufficient.

L1.reasoning: Bounded implementation-granularity match: November19 explicitly models individual dendrites and synapses with spatial/temporal response and fast/slow changes; MCH22 questions sparse inter-neuron messages and asks whether complex cellular machinery must also be simulated.
L1.formal_ceiling: No proved mathematical isomorphism, bisimulation, functor or implementation equivalence; theoretical correspondence is not experimental validation.

L2.reasoning: November computational account -> choose substrate -> model sub-neural and network dynamics -> rendered activity corresponds to MCH hypothesized functionality -> test simulation sufficiency -> possibly increase cellular resolution. Both are proposed requirements, not successful implementations.

L3.reasoning: Reverse from a simulation preserving consciousness-relevant functions: test which intra-cellular/sub-neural details a coarse abstraction omits. November supplies concrete dendritic/synaptic candidates; MCH's broader machinery question does not identify the same minimal sufficient set.
L3.chronological_constraint: Only this exact 2022-11-28T18:09:11-08:00 Git-record-dated formulation is compared against the selected 2026-01-15 target version. Earlier source and target routes remain open; no unique derivation, independent first-publication proof, whole-program firstness or influence follows.

rows.residual: Dendrites and synapses are sub-neural structures, not evidence that every intracellular biochemical process must be simulated. MCH makes a possibility statement, not a proven requirement; neither side demonstrates sufficiency or feasibility.

rows.title: Local interactions can build higher-order organization
rows.conclusion: Micah's November 2022 Git-recorded proposal links context-sensitive local neural components and larger assemblies in a simulated mind. CIMC's reviewed whitepaper also studies how local interactions produce higher-order organization. Its cited pages do not establish the stronger claim that simulation must extend inside neurons.

target.title: Consciousness Is Model Coherence
target.date_type: Selected document-version date, not proof this wording appeared in the initial publication
target.summary: The later whitepaper studies how local interactions create higher-order organization. That supports a local-to-global match, not a claim that this whitepaper requires simulating inside neurons.

rows.shared_subchain: Local interacting computational units, arranged across scales, can be studied or simulated as the basis for higher-order organization.

L1.reasoning: A weaker but genuine multiscale/local-interaction partial: November19 discusses neurons, arrays, edge communities, columns and synchronous groups with context-sensitive responses; CIMC18 studies local units, cells and communities generating global structures, and19 uses distributed messages.
L1.formal_ceiling: No proved mathematical isomorphism, bisimulation, functor or implementation equivalence; theoretical correspondence is not experimental validation.

L2.reasoning: November local spatial/temporal interactions -> assemblies -> rendered system activity shares a local-to-global architecture with CIMC local update rules -> organized dynamics. CIMC's NCA/requests-confirmations implementation does not instantiate November's sub-neural simulation details.

L3.reasoning: Reverse from higher-order organized dynamics: some local interaction rules and component organization must be implemented. November provides a candidate hierarchy; the target output does not force an intra-cellular simulation requirement.
L3.chronological_constraint: Only this exact 2022-11-28T18:09:11-08:00 Git-record-dated formulation is compared against the selected 2026-04-27 target version. Earlier source and target routes remain open; no unique derivation, independent first-publication proof, whole-program firstness or influence follows.

rows.residual: CIMC18-19 neither requires nor explicitly proposes simulating inside a neuron. Processing units, biological cells and agent communities are comparison scales, not evidence of subcellular fidelity. Retain the stronger route open, not established.
